review_notes: I read the whole file and looked at the definitions of archDeriv and casimir1/2/3 in Definitions/Def_LanglandsTunnell_CubicInduction_ArchCentre3.lean. I also checked the sibling files that restate the same lemmas. The file has no @[simp] declarations of its own. The large `attribute [-simp]` and `[-instance]` preambles only switch off lemmas that come from other files, so I did not treat them as defects. I found no rewrite cycles or competing rules. The two findings are about missing simp-normal-form lemmas and about proofs that rebuild them by hand. The first is weaker. Making the lemmas simp could expose `casimirN` to the unfolding lemmas `casimirN_eq` if those were also made simp, so I recommend marking only the `_smul` lemmas. I could not run Lean, so I did not check that the replacements compile or what the downstream simp effects are.

findings.problem: The unconditional scalar-linearity rules `archDeriv i j (c • φ) = c • archDeriv i j φ` and `casimirN (c • w) = c • casimirN w` are not simp lemmas, and the file works around this. `casimir3_smul` does `rw [casimir3_eq, casimir3_eq, Finset.smul_sum]`, then three `Finset.sum_congr` layers with `Finset.smul_sum`, then `rw [D_smul, D_smul, D_smul]`. `D_smul` is applied by hand at every use. The same lemmas, with no simp attribute, are restated in other files of the project (for example `D_smul`, `casimir1_smul`, `casimir2_smul` and `casimir3_smul` in the file about the joint Casimir eigenvector). They also appear as `archDeriv_smul` in several other files. That points to a missing canonical, shared simp rule. At the call sites (the `smul_mem'` field of V and the eigenvalue steps for `archDeriv c₀ d₀ v`) the goals are of the form `casimir1 (a • v) = lam₁ • (a • v)`. Each needs a manual `rw [casimir1_smul, hev.1, smul_comm]` or `rw [..., AsmAux.D_smul]`.
findings.proposed_change: Put `archDeriv_smul` and `casimir1_smul`, `casimir2_smul`, `casimir3_smul` next to the definitions, in Def_LanglandsTunnell_CubicInduction_ArchCentre3 or the WhittakerBlock namespace, and mark them `@[simp]`. Keep the `_eq` unfolding lemmas non-simp, since the file uses `casimirN_eq` in both directions (`rw [← AsmAux.casimir1_eq]`). `D_add` and `casimirN_add` need smoothness hypotheses, so they should stay as explicit lemmas. After that, `casimir3_smul` can be a short `simp [casimir3_eq, Finset.smul_sum, archDeriv_smul]` or can follow directly from a linear-map packaging. The eigenvalue goals then close with `simp [hev.1, smul_comm]`.
findings.benefit: Each file that needs scalar linearity of the Casimir operators no longer re-proves the lemma and rewrites by hand. The file would also lose about 20 lines of nested `Finset.sum_congr` boilerplate. The unconditional rules are safe orientations: the right-hand side moves the scalar outward and the expression gets smaller, so simp cannot loop.

findings.problem: `hsum` states the closure of `Blk` under linear combinations only through `Fin m`-indexed sums and `![...]` vectors. Every consumer then has to convert the instance back to its simp-normal form by hand. For scalar multiplication the same conversion is written three times. The three `have e1/e2/e3 … := by funext …; simp` blocks, followed by `rw [e1, e2, e3] at hb'`, appear inline in `smul_mem'` (around line 449) and again in `hsmulBlk` (line 474 onwards). The addition case in `add_mem'` has an analogous `Fin 2` version. `hsum3` has a third version over `Fin 3`. The reshaping lemmas `e1/e2/e3` are one-off statements about `![a] l * ![v] l g`, so no simp lemma or interface lemma is shared. `smul_mem'` could use `hsmulBlk` if the latter were defined earlier. The `Fin.sum_univ_two` and `Fin.sum_univ_one` simp calls are also repeated.
findings.proposed_change: State `Blk` closure lemmas in their normal forms (`Blk.add`, `Blk.smul`, `Blk.sum`) once, and derive them from `joint_expansion_sum_mul` once. Define `hsmulBlk` before V, with an `a • v` conclusion, and let `smul_mem'` call `hsmulBlk a v (hMcont v hv) cv cv' hb` and `add_mem'` call the analogous `Blk.add`. Also add one lemma, such as `Blk.smul_eq`, that rewrites `Blk ρ δ n J e (fun g => ∑ l : Fin 1, …) …` to the normal form, so downstream proofs do not re-prove `e1/e2/e3`.
findings.benefit: The about 30 duplicated lines of funext/simp reshaping reduce to single applications. The `Fin.sum_univ_*` simp normalisation is done once, so it cannot drift between the copies. Readers see the actual closure properties of `Blk` instead of reshaping noise.
